ai_summary.headline: Yemen's MPC ask is modest at 5.5% of requirements and only a third funded, in a plan 23% funded overall.
ai_summary.narrative: The 2026 HNRP seeks USD 2.16bn for 12 million people, with MPC at USD 119.9m, about 5.5% of requirements [s2]. By late October the plan had received USD 506m, 23% of requirements, while MPC had received USD 35.7m, 30% of its own requirement on FTS's single-cluster view (USD 38.5m, 32%, counting shared flows) [s1][s2]. MPC therefore fares somewhat better than the plan average, though from a small base. A functioning Cash and Markets Working Group publishes MPCA snapshots, and REACH runs a monthly JMMI, although only for government-controlled areas [s5][s7]. A Yemen Donor Cash Forum is operating with CashCap and CALP support funded by FCDO [s6]. We found no published cost-efficiency, modality-preference or recent feasibility data, and no breakdown of voucher or sectoral cash. It appears likely that these gaps, not funding alone, limit the case for scaling cash, but this is inference. Pooled-fund cash shares could not be retrieved.
barriers: Plan only 23% funded; MPC at 30% of its requirement
Market monitoring covers government-controlled areas only
No public cost-efficiency or modality-preference evidence found
CMWG leadership and CashCap role not confirmed
opportunities: Yemen Donor Cash Forum with CALP/CashCap support under the Common Donor Approach
